questions.title: What do you do if your ball goes out of bounds?
questions.question: If your ball goes outside the golf course (out of bounds), what should you do next?

choices.text: Drop a new ball where the old ball went out and keep playing.
Go back to where you hit your last shot, hit another ball, and add one extra shot to your score.
Put your ball back on the course and keep playing with no extra shot.

questions.explanation: If your ball goes out of bounds, you have to go back to where you last hit and play again. You add one extra shot to your score.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: When your ball goes outside the golf course area, usually past white stakes or lines.
An extra shot added to your score when you break a rule.

questions.teachingTip: Walk the player to the boundary, show the white stakes or lines, and explain what out of bounds means. Let them practise replaying a shot and counting the extra stroke.
likelyMisconceptions: Thinking they can just keep playing from out of bounds.
Thinking they can move the ball back onto the course without a penalty.

questions.title: What do you have to do if your ball is out of bounds?
questions.question: If you find out your ball is out of bounds, what should you do next according to the rules?

choices.text: Drop a ball at the spot where your ball went out of bounds and keep playing.
Go back to where you played your last shot, play another ball, and add a one-stroke penalty.
Move the ball back in bounds and keep playing with no penalty.

questions.explanation: When a ball is out of bounds, you must go back to the place you last played from, play again, and add a one-stroke penalty.
